mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a liquidity trap, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters, it signals overconsumption and potential future demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth for 2 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% in 1 month.
